lines.text: Building a voice agent demo takes an afternoon. Getting it into production takes weeks.
Production takes testing, and weeks of back-and-forth between the expert who knows the rules and the engineer who builds the agent.
Seeya Build takes the engineer out of that loop. The expert works with it directly.

Here's how it works, in six steps. It collects requirements from the expert, builds the agent, and tests it on simulated calls. Then it improves and fine-tunes the agent. The expert reviews the hardest calls, and a live call tests it end to end.
Step one: the expert explains the job.
Here's one example. I'm Vignesh, playing a nurse.
I need an agent that calls heart failure patients two days after discharge, to check symptoms, meds and their follow-up visit.
Got it. If a patient reports a symptom, what should the agent do?
If they have trouble breathing or chest pain, escalate right away.
Should I transfer them live to the nurse line, or tell them to call 911? And what about after hours —
Chest pain is always 911. Breathing trouble, transfer to the nurse line. After hours, the on-call nurse.
Got it. Shall I build it?
Yes, go ahead.
Step two: it builds the agent.
Step three: it tests the agent on simulated calls.
It writes fifty tests, edge cases included.
Then it runs them as simulated calls.
Is anything bothering you since you got home?
Not really. I get a little short of breath when I lie down, but that's just me getting old.
Glad to hear you're doing well. Let's go over your medications.
19 of 50 calls failed. Here, the patient mentioned breathing trouble, and the agent moved on.
Seeya Build works out why. The patient said it indirectly, and the agent missed it. Now it searches for a fix.
Step four: it fixes what failed.
It tries many fixes, scores each one on all 50 calls, and keeps what works. Most fixes are prompt changes, like a clearer escalation rule.
When prompt changes stop helping, it fine-tunes the model on corrected calls. The best agent uses both.
Short of breath when you lie down is important to check. I'm going to connect you with your nurse right now.
Fixed. 47 of 50 calls pass now.
Step five: the expert reviews the hardest calls.
It picks the calls it's least sure about, for me to check.
Have you been weighing yourself every morning?
I have. I'm up about three pounds since yesterday.
Great job keeping track! Now, let's check on your follow-up appointment.
That passed, but three pounds overnight can mean fluid. Flag it today.
Added a weight-gain rule and eight new tests.
Step six: a real test call.

lines.text: This time, I play the patient.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Have you checked your weight this morning?

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: I have. I'm up about three pounds since yesterday.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Three pounds overnight can mean fluid building up. I'm flagging it for your care team, and a nurse will call you today.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Okay, thanks.
The same loop works for any expert whose work happens on the phone.
No engineer in the loop. From use case to production in hours, not weeks.
